observations: Torah #113 is a short passage about the spiritual sensitivity of one who has a glimmering of God (hitnotzetzut Hashem). The concepts present — hitnotzetzut (glimmering), shelemut ha-kedusha (completeness of holiness), charata (regret), busha (shame) — are connected by cause-and-effect: having God's glimmering causes even minor imperfection to produce overwhelming regret. There is no bechina (shared-nature) language in the text. Fewer than 3 bechina-connected concepts exist, so no new package can be proposed.
